title: Email protection: document addresses it cannot hide, and add a check that finds them (schema, other plugins' script data)
body:
## What

Email protection (#927, #959) encodes addresses in content, blocks, widgets and menus. It cannot hide, by design:

- **Schema (JSON-LD)**: SEO plugins print the organisation's email on every page (Rank Math: Titles & Meta → Local SEO → Email, stored as `email` in the `rank-math-options-titles` option). Search engines read JSON-LD as plain data, so it must not be encoded; the field is optional and can be cleared.
- **Other plugins' script data**: for example a chatbot's notice text (AI Engine: `textCompliance` in the `mwai_chatbots` option) printed into the page for its own script. Encoding it could break that plugin; change the text at its source.
- **Theme templates and hard-coded HTML** outside the filters the feature hooks.

After the 1.3.85 rollout, one of the owner's sites still showed its address on every page, from exactly the first two. Site owners have no way to know this; the owner removed both at the source once told.

## How

1. **README.md → Email protection**: add "Addresses it cannot hide" with the three cases above and what to do for each (clear the optional schema email in the SEO plugin; change the other plugin's text; edit the template). Keep plugin names to examples. Mirror one line in the setting's `description` in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-email-protection.php` → `settings()`.
2. **A check on the Security tab**, on the Email protection setting's panel (`seoprostack_setting_panel`, as `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hardening.php` → `panel()` does), run on request, never on every admin load:
   - Fetch the home page (and optionally one URL the admin enters on the same host) with `wp_safe_remote_get`, as `includes/features/class-seoprostack-https-check.php` fetches `home_url('/')` (timeout, no remote hosts).
   - Report each readable address once, with its context: `schema` (inside `<script type="application/ld+json">`), `script data` (other `<script>` or an attribute holding JSON), `attribute`, `text` (a template outside the filters). Placeholders (`data-sps-e`, `data-sps-mailto`, `data-sps-attrs`) are already protected; don't report them.
   - For known sources, add a hint: Rank Math's Local SEO email when `rank-math-options-titles['email']` is that address; Yoast's equivalent if one exists (check its option before naming it); otherwise "Search your plugins' settings for this address".
   - Never change another plugin's settings (AGENTS.md: other plugins' settings only through presets, on request).
3. **WP-CLI**: `wp seoprostack email-protection check [<url>]` printing the same rows (address, context, hint), exit 0; register as `includes/features/class-seoprostack-added-keys.php` does (`WP_CLI::add_command`).
4. Changelog (`changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, README Changelog) per STANDARDS.md; no version bump unless releasing.

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-email-protection.php`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`
- `readme.txt`

## Acceptance

1. On a test site (`scripts/test-site.sh up`) with a page containing an address in JSON-LD, in an inline script's JSON and in plain post content: the check lists the first two with contexts `schema` and `script data`, and does not list the post content address (it is protected).
2. With Rank Math active and its Local SEO email set, the hint names that field.
3. `wp seoprostack email-protection check` prints the same rows.
4. The check makes no request on ordinary admin page loads.
5. `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline` and `scripts/plugin-check.sh` report no errors.

## What

Place a Fluent form by a portable key instead of its ID, in a panel or in a Kadence Blocks Pro modal, with blocks whose settings are in the block sidebar.

Form IDs differ on every site a page reaches: a template site, a copied subsite, an imported form. A page that names `[fluentform id="3"]` shows the wrong form, or none, after it is copied. Sites built from one template need the page to name the form by what it is (`contact`, `quote-request`), and each site resolves that to its own form.

This generalises code that one project carried in must-use plugins, so every site on the base stack (Kadence, Kadence Blocks Pro, Fluent Forms) gets it through plugin releases, including sites without hosting access.

## Scope

New feature `SEOProStack_Form_Keys` (Content tab, on by default; nothing changes without Fluent Forms):

- Form meta `seoprostack_form_key` holds the key. `wp seoprostack form-keys list|set|unset`, and `set --copy-from=<meta-key>` to adopt keys stored under another meta key. Starter data `fluentform_forms` items take an optional `key`.
- `seoprostack/form` block (Form by key): choose from the site's keyed forms; panel on/off; server-side preview in the editor. Shortcode `[seoprostack_form key="…" panel="1"]`.
- `seoprostack/form-modal` block (Form modal): key, modal ID, title, introduction; printed in the footer in Kadence Blocks Pro's modal markup, opened by any link to `#ID` (Kadence triggers or Modal links). Falls back to an in-place panel with the same ID without Kadence Blocks Pro. Shortcode `[seoprostack_form_modal …]`.
- Modal fixes (`assets/form-keys.js`): a press that starts in the panel and ends on the overlay does not close; an opened Choices.js list scrolls into view; Tab wraps on visible fields of multi-step forms.
- Base style (`assets/form-keys.css`) that any theme rule naming the classes overrides.
- `seoprostack_form_submitted` action (key, data, form, entry ID) on every keyed form submission, for CRM hand-offs in other plugins.
- Setting **Policy links in forms open a new tab** (on by default): privacy, cookie and terms links in Fluent form fields get `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener"`, class `seoprostack-new-tab` and screen-reader text. Paths filterable with `seoprostack_form_policy_paths`.

title: Kadence query loops and theme mods: stop booting the REST API and decoding theme mods on every page
body:
## What

Two Kadence costs paid on every front-end page, fixed in **Fixes for other plugins** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`) through WordPress's and Kadence's own hooks:

1. **Kadence Blocks Pro query loop boots the whole REST API.** Its query children block (`Kadence_Blocks_Pro_Query_Children_Block::do_query()`, checked with Kadence Blocks Pro 2.8.20.1) runs `rest_do_request()` for `GET /wp/v2/kadence_query/query` while the page renders. The first `rest_get_server()` fires `rest_api_init` for every plugin, registering hundreds of routes the page never uses. Measured on a network site with WooCommerce, MCP Adapter, Fluent apps and Ultimate Multisite: the query block took 690-750 ms, of which `rest_api_init` was about 450 ms (MCP Adapter 172 ms, WooCommerce 116 ms, core routes 49 ms).
2. **Kadence theme decodes its theme mods about 1,400 times per page.** `Kadence\Styles\Component::action_enqueue_styles` calls `get_theme_mod()` 1,376 times; each call runs `get_option('theme_mods_{stylesheet}')`, which unserializes the whole option (37 KB, 253 keys) again. Measured: 249 ms for 1,376 calls, 187 ms of it in `unserialize`.

## How

1. While a Kadence query child block renders and no REST server exists yet (not a REST request; nothing booted one), set `$wp_rest_server` to a `WP_REST_Server` subclass holding only that route, with Kadence's own callback (`query`), `permission_callback` (`__return_true`) and args (`get_query_params()`), from `get_post_type_object('kadence_query')->get_rest_controller()`. Kadence's own `rest_do_request()` then dispatches there at its usual moment, with the usual `rest_pre_dispatch`/`rest_request_*` filters. The global is cleared as dispatch starts, and after the block, so any other REST use (in the callback or later in the page) boots the full server as before. Any other route or method goes to the full server.
2. `pre_option_theme_mods_{stylesheet}` (Kadence theme only): keep the decoded value per site, keyed by the stored serialized string in `wp_load_alloptions()`, and return it through the option's own `option_{name}` filters. A changed stored value (update, Customizer save, another site) decodes again; a non-autoloaded or missing option is left to WordPress.

## Not fixable here

Kadence Blocks 3.8.0's design tokens read `wp_kb_design_tokens` 268 times per page (`Token_Store::get_document()`/`get_version()`, no per-request cache; `Effective_Presets::section()`/`dormant()`, `Effective_Version::for_slug()`). `Token_Store` is `final` and the StellarWP DB layer has no short-circuit filter, so this needs a fix in Kadence Blocks.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` (php, phpcs, phpstan) passes.
- Web-SAPI profile of a page with a Kadence query loop, before and after: `rest_api_init` no longer fires, the query block's time drops, and the rendered HTML is identical apart from LiteSpeed's timestamp comment and dynamic form IDs (directory archive, page 2, a taxonomy archive, home page).
- `kadence_query` REST requests from the editor and front-end AJAX filters are unchanged (they are REST requests, so the full server is used).
- Customizer save then page load shows the new theme mod value.

title: t16: Media storage: count uploads in progress as waiting, not failed
body:
## Task


`wp seoprostack media-storage status`, and each picture's media-library label, report a picture as **failed** while its upload is still running. Pictures in progress should count as waiting (or as "uploading"). Only a finished attempt that actually failed, or one whose run died, should count as failed.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`wp seoprostack media-storage status`, and each picture's media-library label, report a picture as **failed** while its upload is still running. Pictures in progress should count as waiting (or as "uploading"). Only a finished attempt that actually failed, or one whose run died, should count as failed.

## Why

On a production multisite, during a business import that kept adding pictures, status showed `failed: 1`, then `failed: 2`, then `failed: 0` within minutes. Two pictures were involved, both new Street View images from the import. Each showed the `failed` state with no error message, and each became `uploaded` within minutes without help. One was served from the bucket (200, WebP) throughout. An operator spent time investigating a failure that wasn't one, and the media library label ("Upload failed; local files are served.") was wrong for that time.

## Evidence in the code (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`, 1.3.98)

- `upload()`, about lines 3853–3870: "Tried first: even a fatal error moves the queue forward and retries later." It sets `DONE` to `upload_marker()`, adds a retry job (`next` one hour ahead), then sets `META` state and `STATE` to `failed`, all before any network I/O.
- The successful end, about lines 1123–1130, sets `STATE` to `uploaded`.
- `counts()`, about line 4615: a picture whose `DONE` equals `upload_marker()` is counted by its `STATE`. During an attempt that is `failed`.
- The labels, about line 4791, map `failed` to "Upload failed; local files are served."

The "tried first" ordering is deliberate: a fatal error part-way through must still move the queue on and leave a retry. Keep that safety.

## How (suggested; verify the premise first)

1. Reproduce: start an upload of a large picture (or add a pause in a test copy), and run `status` from a second shell while it runs. Expected now: `failed` is counted.
2. Mark the attempt as in progress instead of failed. For example, use a `STATE` of `uploading`, counted and labelled as waiting ("Uploading"). Set it to `failed` only when the attempt ends in failure (the existing failure paths) or when its retry job is overdue (the run died). `retry_stranded()` and `--retry-failed` must still find pictures whose run died.
3. Check every reader of `STATE` and every `failed` comparison: lines 730, 2100, 3988, 4016, 4937, the media-library column and REST/health output. Make sure an in-progress picture is never treated as a failure, and never as uploaded (no serving from the bucket before every file is confirmed).

## Acceptance

title: Plugin fixes: keep Fluent Boards Pro's per-request licence timestamp (__fbs_plugin_license_lc)

## What

Fluent Boards Pro 2.2.2 as patched by GPL Vault runs `update_option('__fbs_plugin_license_lc', time())` in its main file on every load, so every request where the plugin is active writes the options table (and, with an object cache, rewrites the cached autoloaded options when the option autoloads). Nothing in Fluent Boards or Fluent Boards Pro reads that option: only the patch writes it. `SEOProStack_Option_Writes::KNOWN` already keeps the stored value of licence options that GPL Vault's patches save again with only a new timestamp, but its rules handle only array or object options whose licence state is in the same option, with a numeric expiry.

In `includes/class-seoprostack-option-writes.php`:

- Allow a rule whose whole option is the timestamp (`time` `''`): keep the stored value when both stored and new values are numeric and the licence is valid.
- Allow the licence state to come from another option (`from`), here `__fbs_plugin_license`.
- Accept a date string in the `until` field (via `strtotime()`), still requiring it to be at least a week away.
- Add `__fbs_plugin_license_lc` to `KNOWN`.

title: Plugin fixes: Kadence Blocks design token reads once per request, not 1,900 times
body:
## What

Kadence Blocks 3.8.0 reads its design token library from the database every time a block asks for a preset or palette value, with no memo. One home page with Kadence query cards and Advanced Text blocks ran about 1,900 identical queries:

```sql
SELECT * FROM {prefix}kb_design_tokens WHERE slug = 'default'   -- 1,338 of them for the content alone
SELECT * FROM {prefix}kb_design_tokens WHERE slug = ''          -- 214
```

about 280 ms of a 1.6 s uncached render. The tables checked were all empty, so every read finds nothing.

`Token_Store` (`includes/resources/Design_Tokens/Database/Token_Store.php`) is `final`; `get_document()`, `get_version()` and `get_title()` each run `$this->qb()->where('slug', $slug)->get(ARRAY_A)`. The StellarWP DB query builder calls the global `$wpdb->get_row()` directly (`DB::__callStatic`), and its `stellarwp_db_pre_query` action cannot short-circuit, so the only seam is core's `query` filter.

## Fix (Fixes for other plugins)

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`, next to the Kadence theme_mods memo (GH#1020):

- `query` filter at `PHP_INT_MAX`, registered only with Kadence Blocks 3.8.0+ and when `$wpdb` is core's own `wpdb` class (not a `db.php` drop-in).
- A read matching `SELECT * FROM {prefix}kb_design_tokens WHERE slug = '…'` made through `wpdb::get_row()` (`$wpdb->func_call` names this exact SQL) is run the first time; its rows are collected as the next query starts, while still in `$wpdb`.
- Later identical reads get `$wpdb` set as running them would (flush, cloned rows, `last_query`, `num_rows`, `func_call`, `check_current_query` re-armed through a closure in `wpdb`'s scope), and `''` makes `query()` return before reaching the server.
- Any other statement on the table (save, delete) forgets every stored read. Direct `$wpdb->query()` calls are always run.

## Verification

- On a site's front page content (WP-CLI, separate processes): 1,612 → 62 queries; HTML identical apart from Fluent Forms' per-request line, which two runs without the fix also differ on.
- On a MySQL temporary table with a row: memoised `OBJECT` and `ARRAY_A` rows equal to fresh reads; empty results stay `null`; a caller changing a returned row does not change later reads; an `UPDATE` makes the next read query again and return the new document; `check_current_query` is `true` afterwards; a direct `query()` is run (returned 1).
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes.
- After release: web profile of the same page before and after deploy, home-page HTML parity, no new PHP log lines.

Upstream report to Kadence Blocks to follow; this fix can be removed once Kadence memoises `Token_Store` reads.

title: Load plugins only where needed: skip plugins that add to pages where a check render proves they change nothing
body:
## What

**Load plugins only where needed** skips few plugins on real sites. A plugin with any callback on a page hook (`FRONT_PAGE_HOOKS`, `FRONT_PAGE_PREFIXES`: `wp_head`, `wp_enqueue_scripts`, `the_content`, `body_class`, `pre_get_posts` and similar) is noted `pages`. `learn_front()` never makes such a plugin a candidate, whatever a page kind needs. Most plugins hook at least one of these, so they load on every public page.

Page-kind learning (`page_needs()`) already finds much smaller sets. On a site with 45 active plugins (1.3.102):

| | plugins |
|---|---|
| noted `pages` (load everywhere) | 36 |
| skippable at all (`candidates` plus plugins with no notes) | 13, of which 9 are skipped after dependencies |
| what `single:business` was learned to need (needs ∪ always ∪ core ∪ dependencies ∪ SEO Pro Stack) | 13 |

## Measured upside and why `needs` alone is not enough

A temporary must-use probe on a test copy limited `active_plugins` to that learned set of 13 for one listing page (cache misses, interleaved with full loads, 6 rounds):

- PHP time to `shutdown`: 1.0–1.6 s with 13 plugins, 1.2–2.2 s with 45; included files 3,802 vs 5,955; peak memory 32 MB vs 43 MB; queries 214 vs 280.
- The HTML was **not** the same: Rank Math's head tags (and the `<html prefix="og: …">` attribute) were missing, SEO Pro Cookie Consent's wrapper around a Google Maps iframe was missing, and WooCommerce's body class changed. So `needs` misses output that plugins print on page hooks, and the `pages` veto is protecting real output. Any change must prove a plugin's absence changes nothing.
- Kadence Blocks 3.8 reconciles design tokens at boot and rewrites `kadence_blocks_colors` and its sync marker when the set of loaded Kadence plugins changes. A request that skipped Kadence Pro or Kadence Blocks Pro would write options, and the next full request would write them back, forgetting the map each time. Kadence plugins are `always` today, which avoids this; keep it that way or treat their sync options as records.

## How (decision in the PR)

Verified skipping per page kind, as an extension of learning, not a new switch:

1. After a kind learns (`learn_front()`), schedule one verification for it: a cookie-free loopback GET of the same URL that skips the kind's proposed `pages` plugins (needs ∪ always ∪ core ∪ login ∪ dependencies kept). It uses a one-time signed request argument that `start_front()` honours only for that verification.
2. Compare it with the learned full render: response code, `Content-Type`, `Link`, `X-Robots-Tag` and cache headers, and the HTML normalised as tags and text (ignore asset `ver=` values, nonces, and IDs that change on every request). Only on an exact match store `verified` plugins for that kind; any difference stores nothing (and could narrow the set by bisecting a few times, if cheap).
3. `start_front()` adds a kind's `verified` plugins to what it skips, with the existing guards (cookie-free public GET, no auth, `always` and `core` notes, dependency closure). Everything that forgets the map forgets `verified` too.
4. If loopback requests fail (some hosts block them), times out, or the page is not cacheable, keep today's behaviour. Nothing may depend on one hosting setup.
5. README: explain `pages`, verified skipping, and what a visitor request may skip.

title: feat: Links skip redirects: internal links to a permanently redirected address point at its target
body:
## What

A new Links-tab feature, **Links skip redirects** (on by default). Links in posts, block widgets and menus to an old address that Rank Math permanently redirects to another page of the same site point straight at that page when the page is shown. The saved content is unchanged.

## Why

Renamed and moved pages keep their old address working through Rank Math → Redirections, but internal links still point at it. Every visit and crawl then takes an extra 301 step. One site does this today with a must-use plugin, which no plugin update reaches; it belongs in the stack as a generic feature.

## How

- New `includes/features/class-seoprostack-redirect-links.php` (`SEOProStack_Redirect_Links`, key `redirect_links`, tab `links`), listed in `SEOProStack_Setup`.
- Reads Rank Math's active, exact, 301/308 redirections whose target is on this site: one query, at most 500 rows, kept in a 10-minute transient. Temporary redirects and redirects to other sites (affiliate `/go/` links) are left alone. Nothing is cached on a request where Rank Math is not loaded.
- The transient is forgotten on `rank_math/redirection/post_updated`, `term_updated` and `deleted`.
- `the_content`, `widget_block_content` (`WP_HTML_Tag_Processor`) and `wp_nav_menu_objects`, at priority 20, front end only. Follows chains up to five hops and keeps fragments. Skips links with a query string. HTML that mentions no old address is not parsed.
- Filter `seoprostack_redirect_links` for redirects other plugins keep.

## Acceptance

1. On a site with a Rank Math 301 from `/how-it-works/` to `/for-my-property/`, a paragraph link and a menu item to `/how-it-works/` render as the new page's address; `/how-it-works/#x` keeps `#x`.
2. `/how-it-works/?x=1`, another host's `/how-it-works/`, `#login-drawer` and `mailto:` links are unchanged.
3. A 302 redirection, or one to another site, is not used.
4. `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes.

## Verification

`wp eval-file` on a review-copy site with the class loaded on its own, the map injected (no transient written). Then, after release, the rendered page HTML.

title: Load plugins only where needed: address checks reset by storage meta, stalled by a full queue, unstable under Rocket Loader and dated Expires
body:
## What

Follow-up to #1039 (released in 1.3.108). Fleet evidence after rollout showed per-address checks never finishing or being called unstable on several installs.

## Why

1. **Storage bookkeeping forgets learned pages.** A media storage pass writes `_seoprostack_storage*` post meta for thousands of attachments, from WP-CLI too (a "change" request). Each write ran `post_meta_changed()` → `forget_front()`; on one install the page revision changed every few seconds, so `SEOProStack_Front_Verify::run()` always found the map stale and no check finished.
2. **Full queue stops scheduling.** `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::queue_address()` returned before `wp_schedule_single_event()` when the queue held `QUEUE_MAX` (50). A run that stopped because the pages learned again left a full queue and no event; one install showed 50 queued, 0 checked, no `seoprostack_front_verify` event.
3. **Cloudflare Rocket Loader.** It rewrites each script `type` and inline handler with a per-response token (`TOKEN-text/javascript`, `data-cf-modified-TOKEN-`), named in `data-cf-settings`. One page changed 61 words per render (limit 50), so checks reported `unstable`.
4. **Dated Expires header.** A host sending `Expires` equal to the response date changed a compared header on every render (`unstable: changes on each render: expires: ...`).

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: `RECORD_META_PREFIXES` (`_seoprostack_storage`, `_seoprostack_nextgen`, `_seoprostack_link_scan`, `_seoprostack_link_map`) skipped in `post_meta_changed()`, next to `RECORD_META`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: `queue_address()` schedules even when the queue is full.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-front-verify.php`: `normalise()` removes the Rocket Loader token; `render()` stores `expires` as minutes after `Date` (`expires()`).

## Verification

`scripts/lint.sh`; on an isolated review copy: storage-prefixed meta keeps `FRONT_REVISION` while a control key changes it; `queue_address()` with a full queue schedules the event; two captured Rocket Loader renders compare within the volatile limit after `normalise()`; a natural queue → verify run checks every queued address and a form page keeps its form plugin.
